# Entropy-Controlled Quantum Simulation

> Scientific account of how entropy-decrease capacity of known target controls governs the oracle-query cost of simulating Hermitian reflection noise.

## Entry points

- [Repository overview](README.md): principal results, proof navigation, verification, and scope.
- [Scientific index](science/README.md): connected proof route and navigation by question.
- [Model and results](science/model.md): precise target descriptor, total exposure, controlled-reflection oracle, unconditioned diamond error, and resource promises.

## Reading routes

- Story: begin with the model, then interpretation and the exact mixed-reset example; use the query proof to connect the physical mechanism to simulation cost.
- Study: use the [learning overview](learning/README.md), [Watrous bridge](learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md), and [30-milestone map](learning/MILESTONES.md). The map has 10 background/preliminary targets and 20 narrative/innovation targets, each with dependencies, conceptual connections, and canonical sources.
- Theorems: go directly to channel stability for the general Hermitian-jump bound and query complexity for the fixed-dimension classification.
- Reproduction: follow verification/README.md, requirements.txt, and verification/checks.py; the expected JSON records the documented finite cases.

## Educational anchor

John Watrous, [The Theory of Quantum Information (2018)](https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~watrous/TQI/), is the single educational anchor. The bridge selects relevant sections, translates notation and normalization, and explains the additional dynamics, control-budget, and oracle-query steps supplied by the project. Primary research dependencies remain identified in the scientific account and bibliography.

## Authoritative science

- [Entropy-decrease capacity](science/entropy_capacity.md): definition, reference invariance, additivity, composition, and exact reset capacities.
- [Channel stability](science/channel_stability.md): complete Hermitian-jump perturbation proof using entropy production and backward variance, including controls and singular states.
- [Mixed resets](science/mixed_resets.md): exact two-qubit fixed-rate witness for every real exposure time and capacity regime.
- [Query complexity](science/query_complexity.md): bounded-query unitary-learning upper, global-phase fit, Poisson cap, and ordinary-oracle hybrid lower.
- [Memory and local noise](science/memory_and_local_noise.md): dimension sharpness, local GHZ example, local query law, and weighted retained-qubit/pure-reset construction.
- [Interpretation](science/interpretation.md): physical meaning and boundaries of the results.

## Evidence and attribution

- [Related work](references/RELATED_WORK.md): primary-source comparison and the scope of imported results.
- [Bibliography](references/references.bib): machine-readable bibliographic metadata.
- [Finite verification](verification/README.md): commands, grids, tolerances, reference environment, and limitations.
- [Verification script](verification/checks.py): reproducible finite matrix and witness checks.
- [Reference numerical outputs](verification/expected_results.json): a recorded successful run.

## Conventions that affect interpretation

Entropy is measured in nats. Trace and diamond norms are unhalved. Every initial, intermediate, and terminal target control is charged. The retained dimension includes persistent quantum and classical memory; an untouched reference is allowed. The target budget is separate from simulator memory and reset use.

The main query theorem fixes target dimension four and diamond error 0.01. It counts bounded calls to the unknown controlled reflection, not total runtime. The general channel bound uses a supplied matched Hermitian-jump representation. The supporting long-time weighted-memory construction reduces actual dissipative activity; it does not provide the corresponding stronger lower bound for raw reflection queries.

The analytical proofs are authoritative for universal claims. The finite numerical suite checks its documented examples and identities. The account makes no quantum-Fisher-information or work-cost claim.
